crossModuleLinks.admissionRule: A writable link requires both endpoints to resolve to the same verified Store; a read-only link must not hydrate a foreign Store endpoint. An uncertified endpoint keeps shared admission disabled.

background.rule: Every continuation, event, index document, relation, query, rebuild, replay, and full sync must retain one verified Store and fail closed when shared Store provenance is absent.

invariants: The canonical Product module remains the only owner of catalog persistence and behavior.
Every explicit Product entity receives immutable Store ownership at creation.
Implicit pivot ownership is derived from both parents and both parents must share one Store.
Shared placement requires transaction-local Store context before any Product persistence access.
Dedicated placement derives Store context only from its immutable placement binding.
List, count, pagination, search, graph, import, export, and index paths scope before reading or ordering.
Global product options are global only inside one Store.
Store ownership never comes from an untrusted request body, filter, selector, or event payload.
Owner reassignment and transaction Store rebinding are rejected.
Public Medusa contracts and entity identifiers remain compatible.
A cross-module link is unavailable in shared placement until both resource endpoints are certified.
Completing the Product phase family does not enable shared production while linked modules remain uncertified.

7G-5C.owner: canonical Product module service plus central MedusaService manager hooks

7G-5D.owner: workflow continuation context and Index module

7G-5E.owner: central module-link endpoint validation and two-mode proof

attackMatrix.proof: Shared CRUD without verified Store context is denied.
Same-Store CRUD succeeds through canonical Product services.
Foreign IDs cannot be retrieved, listed, counted, or paginated.
Client-supplied store_id is ignored or rejected and never changes ownership.
Owner reassignment and transaction Store rebinding are denied.
Different Stores may use the same product, category, and collection handles.
Different Stores may use the same tag, type, global-option title, and variant identifiers.
A same-Store duplicate for each Store-scoped unique key is denied.
Category parent and tree traversal cannot cross Stores.
Product type and collection relationships cannot cross Stores.
Product-to-category and product-to-tag pivots cannot cross Stores.
Product option, value, and product-option relationships cannot cross Stores.
Variant, option-value, image, and variant-image relationships cannot cross Stores.
Global options can be shared only by Products in the same Store.
Soft delete, restore, cascades, and compensation retain the original Store.
Raw Knex and native-delete paths cannot bypass Store scoping.
Import continuations retain the initiating Store across pause and resume.
Import resume under a different or absent Store is denied.
Export emits only catalog records owned by the active Store.
Product events retain verified Store provenance and replay idempotently.
Index documents and relations are Store-namespaced.
Index queries and pagination cannot return a foreign Store document.
Index full sync and rebuild require an explicit Store partition.
Product-to-Price-Set links reject either foreign endpoint.
Product links to Inventory, Sales Channel, and Shipping Profile reject foreign endpoints.
Read-only Cart, Order, and Translation links cannot hydrate foreign Product data.
Dedicated placement works without request Store context and rejects a mismatched context.
Shared database role and direct SQL without transaction Store context are denied by RLS.
Implicit pivot insert, update, and delete fail when parents or context disagree.
Concurrent Store A and Store B operations never exchange Product ownership.
Upgrade backfill proves row counts, ownership counts, and stable catalog digests.
Rollback evidence restores the pre-change schema without leaving partial enforcement.
